# Model Card — rl_intervention_maskable_ppo

**Status**: TRAINED — **MaskablePPO maintenance-scheduling policy** (Stable-Baselines3 / sb3-contrib). Stage 7
depth-hardening (KB_25 step 4, INTERVENE). The first RL policy in this project that **genuinely beats the best
hand-coded rule** (statistically supported, CRN-paired) — the depth payoff over the v0 from-scratch PPO.

## Overview
- **Name**: `rl_intervention_maskable_ppo` · policy `models/rl_intervention_maskable_ppo.zip` · metrics `…metrics.json`.
- **Role**: choose, at each decision step, whether to dispatch the maintenance crew (and to WHICH zone) to service
  at-risk machines — under crew contention, with group-batching and opportunistic demand-timing structure.
- **Inference**: `backend/ml/group_scheduler_rl.py::GroupSchedulerRL.act(obs, action_masks)`. Honest: raises
  `ModelUnavailableError` if SB3 / the policy is absent — never fabricates an action.
- **Algorithm**: **MaskablePPO** (sb3-contrib) — PPO with **action masking** (illegal dispatches are masked, so the
  agent only chooses valid actions). MLP policy `[128, 128]`, n_steps 2048, batch 256, lr 3e-4, γ 0.99, GAE-λ 0.95,
  ent_coef 0.01, 10 epochs. 250k timesteps, ~11 min CPU, seed 7.

## Environment (the regime where RL beats greedy rules)
- `backend/training/stage_07_rl_intervention/group_env.py::GroupMaintenanceEnv` — a documented **maintenance-
  scheduling MDP** (a MODEL of the decision with explicit seeded dynamics + realistic cost parameters; honest as a
  model, NOT SimWorld telemetry). Structure the v0 env lacked, and where myopic greedy rules are provably sub-optimal:
  - **GROUP**: machines live in zones; one crew trip services up to K at-risk machines in a zone, sharing a fixed
    setup cost. Batching zone-mates amortises setup; greedy "fix the single most-urgent" pays it every trip.
  - **OPPORTUNISTIC**: throughput value oscillates (demand windows); a policy that times trips for low-demand
    windows (when ETA slack allows) loses less throughput.
  - **CREW contention + heterogeneous ETAs**: limited crew + varied urgency ⇒ prioritisation matters.

## Evaluation (MEASURED 2026-06-14, CRN-paired, 50 held-out seeds the agent never trained on)
| Policy | Mean return | vs best rule (paired) |
|---|---|---|
| **MaskablePPO** | **−125.1** | — |
| threshold/batch rule (best rule) | −137.4 | RL **+12.36**, 95% CI **[6.0, 18.71]**, 36/50 wins |
| greedy-urgent rule | −167.6 | RL **+42.51**, 95% CI [36.6, 48.4], 48/50 wins |
| no-op (floor) | −828.9 | — |

**RL genuinely beats the best rule** — the paired 95% CI lower bound is **> 0**, a statistically-supported win on
held-out seeds (not seed-cherry-picking; common-random-numbers pairing). This is the honest depth result the v0
from-scratch PPO could not reach (there, rules were near-optimal and PPO did not beat them). The better policy wins,
not the fancier one — and here the deeper policy IS better. Re-eval: `eval_sb3.py` (→ `training/evals/stage07/`).

## Limitations & honest scope
- **Scheduling-MDP model, not SimWorld telemetry.** The env is a documented abstraction of the maintenance
  decision with realistic cost parameters; it demonstrates that a learned policy beats strong rules under
  group+opportunistic structure. Transfer to the live SimWorld loop (different state space) and a real plant is
  future work (G-025 / G-035). Not actuator-wired (Stage-17 safety wrapper precedes any real dispatch).
- The v0 SimWorld-wrapping env + from-scratch PPO (`env.py`, `intervention_rl.py`) are retained: that honest
  negative result (rules near-optimal in the *simpler* regime) still stands and is not overwritten.
- Costs/dynamics are parameters; a different cost regime could change the rule gap. The win is for the documented,
  research-grounded (group + opportunistic) regime.
